deep.reconstruction:
The page is an organizing table of contents: 'Les douze avatars principaux de la Tour de Teichmüller'. The crossed-out first phrase is 'systèmes de groupoïdes'. The replacement says the avatars are groupoids 'RTD…' (presumably the reduced/special decorated Teichmüller groupoids S_*TD of the next page). They come with discrete structures, the operations of surgery catalogued on the previous page: sum, erasing markings, cutting, gluing, filling holes. The most intrinsic representative is Π_top.

The left column is a vertical chain of comparison functors, from the most combinatorial model at the bottom to the most topological at the top. The right column is annotated with the corresponding kind of 'chirurgie' (surgery): top., diff., C-an., hyp.

The twelve avatars:
1. Π_top: compact oriented topological surfaces with boundary; morphisms are isotopy classes of homeomorphisms (made precise on p.43).
2. Π_diff: differentiable surfaces with smooth boundary.
3. Π'_diff: smooth surfaces with marked points and tangent directions at them, 'conformes', i.e. up to conformal/real-blow-up data. Linked to Π_diff by a pair of arrows (an equivalence), via real blow-up of a marked point with a direction to a boundary circle with a base point.
4. Π_an: complex-analytic (Riemann) surfaces with C^∞ boundary.
5. Π'_an: the punctured analytic analogue, again ⇄ Π_an.
6. Π_hyp: hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundary.
7. Π'_hyp: presumably cusped/punctured hyperbolic surfaces, with Π'_hyp → Π'_an.
8. Π_Calg: complex algebraic curves, 'courbes MD' (Mumford–Deligne stable curves), with some datum at the double points (word unclear, transcribed 'propagation des ressorts'; likely tangential/smoothing data on the two branches), plus marked points.
9. Π_Q̄-alg: the same over Q̄. This is where Gal(Q̄/Q) acts on the tower.
10. Π_comb: combinatorial model via maps ('cartes', i.e. ribbon graphs) with boundary cycles and marked vertices.
11. Π_Lego: the 'Teichmüller Lego' of the Esquisse, built from the basic pieces of the game.
12. Π_P: the 'pantalonique' model whose only pieces are pairs of pants; 'pantalons' is corrected to 'triades'.

Purpose: to assert that one and the same object, the Teichmüller tower (the system of mapping-class groupoids with gluing/cutting operations), has transcendental, hyperbolic, algebro-geometric, arithmetic (Q̄) and purely combinatorial incarnations. Comparing them is what lets Gal(Q̄/Q) act on a combinatorially presented tower (the Esquisse programme). The next page begins the detailed treatment with T_top, T^±_top and the signature morphism to [±1].
errors: Not an error, but a gap: the arrows are only asserted. The page does not say whether they are equivalences of groupoids, equivalences of 'towers' compatible with the surgery operations, or merely functors. Only the horizontal ⇄ pairs are marked as two-way.

The arrow Π_comb → Π_Q̄-alg is not canonical as stated. Passing from maps/ribbon graphs to Q̄-curves needs a Belyi/Strebel-type construction and choices, and functoriality for isotopy classes needs justification.

Π_Calg is described using stable (MD) curves, which include degenerate objects. Its morphisms then cannot simply be isotopy classes of homeomorphisms. Some 'fundamental groupoid at infinity / tangential base point at the nodes' formalism is implicitly required, and the unclear datum at double points is presumably meant to supply it; this is left unspecified.

ideas.what: The Teichmüller tower as a system of groupoids with surgery operations (gluing, cutting, erasing markings), whose most intrinsic model is the topological mapping-class groupoid
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller tower / modular operad of mapping class groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984); formalized later by Moore–Seiberg (1989), Bakalov–Kirillov (2000), Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000)

ideas.what: Equivalence of boundary circles with marked points plus tangent directions (Π_diff ⇄ Π'_diff, Π_an ⇄ Π'_an, Π_hyp ⇄ Π'_hyp)
ideas.modern_name: real oriented blow-up / tangential base points; framed (decorated) punctures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov and others for framed moduli
ideas.where_published: Esquisse alludes to tangent directions at points; not in this explicit form as far as I know

ideas.what: Hyperbolic model with geodesic boundary as an avatar of the tower
ideas.modern_name: hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundary; Fenchel–Nielsen / Teichmüller space with boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Fenchel–Nielsen, Thurston); tower viewpoint later in Mirzakhani-era and Penner-type work

ideas.what: Algebraic model via Mumford–Deligne stable curves over C and over Q̄ with data at nodes, so Gal(Q̄/Q) acts on the tower
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory; Galois action on π1 of M̄_{g,n} at tangential base points at infinity

ideas.what: Combinatorial model via maps (ribbon graphs) with boundary cycles and marked vertices
ideas.modern_name: ribbon-graph / fat-graph model of mapping class groupoids (cf. dessins d'enfants)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Harer, Penner, Kontsevich (1980s–1992); Grothendieck for dessins

ideas.what: Teichmüller Lego model and pants-only ('pantalonique', triades) model
ideas.modern_name: Lego–Teichmüller game; pants complex / Hatcher–Thurston presentation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, Lego); Hatcher–Thurston (1980), Moore–Seiberg (1989), Bakalov–Kirillov (2000), Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000)

missed.claim: An explicit catalogue of twelve models of the Teichmüller tower, linked by a chain of comparison functors from the pants-only combinatorial model up to the topological one. Each model is paired with its own kind of surgery (top., diff., C-an., hyp.), and primed variants with marked points plus tangent directions are equivalent to the bordered versions. The Esquisse names several of these models, but this systematic ladder, with surgery compatibility at each level, does not appear in the literature as a single comparison theorem.
missed.quote: Les douze avatars principaux de la Tour de Teichmüller
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modern GT theory uses various of these models piecemeal (ribbon graphs, pants complex, stable curves with tangential base points). A uniform statement that all twelve are equivalent as towers with surgery operations, e.g. as modular operads in groupoids, would be a clean foundational result that is still only partially written down.

missed.claim: The hyperbolic-with-geodesic-boundary model is placed explicitly in the Galois/anabelian tower between the analytic and algebraic models, with 'hyperbolic surgery' as a structure on it.
missed.quote: cas hyperboliques (à bord géodésiques) ... ch. hyp.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Links Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory to hyperbolic gluing (Fenchel–Nielsen twists, Mirzakhani-style cut-and-glue). The hyperbolic side is rarely used in GT work.

deep.surprise_reason: The models themselves are mostly in the Esquisse or the later literature, but this explicit twelve-step ladder with surgery types and primed tangent-direction variants is an unpublished organizational detail. It is a programme sketch, not a result.
